correctness.rationale: The proof uses the source's minimal H-description and works in the correct codimension-two Euclidean affine space. For n>=3, the 2n coordinate facets alone give the sharp global upper bound and force the proposed center if equality holds. At that center, every facet distance is computed exactly. Writing u=|S\T|, v=|T\S|, w=|S∩T| and Q=n^2-w^2-(u-v)^2 yields projected-normal norm squared Q/(2n), slack Q/4+w/n, and distance sqrt(nQ/8)+w sqrt(2/(nQ)). The cases w>=1 and w=0 give a strict global minimum exactly at the coordinate facets. The n=2 six-facet calculation independently gives radius 1 and the full center segment.

value.rationale: The harmonic polytope is a canonical object arising from the conormal geometry of matroids and has an established literature on faces, volumes, and local vertex structure. The inradius is a natural realization-sensitive size invariant. The theorem gives it exactly in every rank, determines all optimal centers, and proves that for n>=3 only 2n coordinate facets among 3^n-3 total facets control the maximal ball. The rank-two transition from a one-dimensional Chebyshev-center locus to unique higher-rank centers adds structural content beyond a single closed formula.
